title: Word Search
kidExplanation: A letter grid like a word search puzzle. Can your finger trace the word without reusing a square?
plainProblem: Word Search: A letter grid like a word search puzzle. Worked example — input: board = [["A","B","C","E"],["S","F","C","S"],["A","D","E","E"]], word = "ABCCED"; expected output: true. Why: Path exists. Interview pattern to name out loud: Backtracking (try → explore → undo).

thinkingSteps.title: Why it is slow
thinkingSteps.body: Count the nested work. If each choice restarts a full scan, time blows up. Name the cost before optimizing — interviewers want that honesty. Target after the insight: See code.

thinkingSteps.title: Aha insight
thinkingSteps.body: To determine if a given word exists in the 2D board, we can perform a depth-first search (DFS) from each cell in the board. At each cell, we check if the current character of the word matches the character in the cell. If it does, we mark the cell as visited, recursively search its neighboring cells, and backtrack if the search is unsuccessful. We repeat this process for all cells in the board.
